clues: This town lies in the inner part of Minas Gerais, a state in the south east of Brazil. It sits east of the state capital, Belo Horizonte.
Rain here falls mostly from October to April, and December is the wettest month. In the dry season, dry air and fumes build up and spoil the air.
In 1921, a steel company set up in this place. The town grew and grew because of that steel works.
The most grand house in town was built to house the pioneer the town is named for. It stands by the old Catalan Forge, a sight people come to see.
The town's best known church was built in the 1940s and is named for Saint Joseph the Worker. It is called the Mother Church by local people.
